title: Name Descriptors
html:
The last word on a generated item is a Superior postfix. On green gear that word is how you read STR / AGI / END / INT. Magic and Unique add a prefix. Rare can add another postfix in front of the Superior word. Full stack: Modifiers. Mythic extra endings: Mythic Suffixes.

From items/mg/SwordMG.gc: Magic = Magic + Item + Binder + Superior; Rare adds a Rare postfix; Unique uses a Unique prefix instead of Magic. Yellow is not “prefix instead of last word.”

The old wiki listed most of these words. Names marked client were missing from the recovered page. Checked against the client ModPAL files.

Armor

Any class can wear any armor that meets the level requirement. The postfix still comes from the armor's class palette.

Fighter

  • Beetle — END
  • Hippo — STR
  • Penguin, Ant, Liger — STR, END
  • Tigon, Panda, Tarantula — STR, AGI

Ranger

  • Hawk — AGI
  • Greyhound — END
  • Manatee, Newt, Bonobo — AGI, END
  • Dragonfly, Squid, Blowfish — AGI, INT

Mage

  • Noggin' — INT
  • Turtle — END
  • Starfish, Armadillo, Unicorn, Wallaby — END, INT
  • Narwhal — AGI, INT (client exception: mythic ninja mage body only, not random drops)

Weapons

Weapon postfixes sit on a specific weapon family, which is why they line up with crushing / piercing / slashing and melee / ranged.

Melee

Crushing

Maces

  • Snapper — END
  • Bunny — AGI, END
  • Hog — STR, END
  • Buckaroo — AGI, END, INT
  • Hippopotamus — AGI, STR (client; not the same as armor Hippo)

Staves

  • Platypus — INT
  • Wombat — END, INT
  • Beaver — STR, END, INT

Piercing

Picks

  • Taint — STR (client)
  • Hysteria — AGI, END
  • Rage — STR, END
  • Battle — STR, END, INT

Slashing

Swords

  • Bovine — AGI
  • Muskrat — AGI, INT
  • Nutria — STR, INT
  • Monkey — AGI, END, INT

Axes

  • Rendezvous Point — AGI
  • Reactor — STR
  • Party — AGI, END
  • Ghetto — STR, END
  • Nether Region — AGI, STR (client)
  • Flipside — STR, AGI, INT

Ranged

Piercing

Crossbows

  • Sugar Glider — AGI
  • Roadkill — END (the old wiki put this under guns as END, INT; the client is crossbow END only)
  • Ladybug — AGI, INT
  • Gerbil — END, INT
  • Wasp — AGI, END, INT

Slashing

Guns

  • Yeti — AGI
  • Termite — END, INT
  • Spammer — AGI, END, INT

Cannons

These were not on the recovered wiki page. Two-handed cannons use the same palette.

  • Jumbo Shrimp — AGI
  • Elephant — END
  • Brontosaurus — STR
  • Whale — AGI, END
  • Rhino — END, INT (same word as jewelry Rhino, different stats)
  • Kraken — AGI, INT
  • Python — AGI, END, INT

The shared weapon palette also names Dik-Dik (AGI, END, STR) as a Superior postfix, marked new, but no weapon family actually rolls it.

Jewelry

Rings and amulets share the same Superior postfix list, except Chicken, which is amulet-only.

  • Crocodile — END
  • Sasquatch — STR
  • Jackalope — AGI
  • Dodo — INT
  • Clam — STR, END
  • Llama — AGI, END
  • Chicken — AGI, END (client; amulets only)
  • Amoeba — AGI, STR (client)
  • Donkey — AGI, INT
  • Rooster — END, INT
  • Rhino — STR, INT
  • Chinchilla — STR, AGI, END
  • Butterfly — AGI, END, INT
  • Lobster — STR, END, INT
  • Goat — AGI, INT, STR (client)
  • Algae — STR, AGI, END, INT (client)

Prefixes

The old page only listed a few preceding adjectives. In the client those words are Magic/Rare rolls, not the Superior last-word list:

  • Stitching — +Piercing (jewelry Rare postfix, not a prefix)
  • Carving — +Slashing
  • Slugging — +Melee damage (jewelry Rare postfix)
  • Molten — +Fire (armor Magic prefix is +Fire and +Melee)
  • Revived — health regen

Beyond that the client has a large named-mod pool: about 240 Magic prefixes, 320 Unique prefixes, plus Rare resist/crit/speed words and three Mythic prefixes (Bloodlusting, Steam Rolling, Up-Sized). Mythic armor also uses joke parenthetical postfixes such as (Do Not Iron) and (May Catch Fire and Explode).

Those extra names are real, but they are not the “read the last word for STR/AGI/END/INT” system. Dumping every one here would just be a phone book.

Superior postfix list and the prefix counts come from the client ModPAL files.
